TerrainDesc.village: Settlement. You can rest at an inn and restock IP.
TerrainDesc.city: Large settlement with shops and travel services.
TerrainDesc.camp: Protected area: a safe place to rest in the wilds.
TerrainDesc.sea: Needs a vessel. Allow passage on the card or the terrain.
TerrainDesc.ruins: Point of interest: remains of something old.
TerrainDesc.dungeon: Point of interest: a dungeon entrance.

rest.name: Rest
rest.desc:
The group rests for 4 to 6 hours. Each PC recovers all HP and MP and recovers from all status effects.
In the wilds you need a magic tent, someone's hospitality or a safe place; in settlements, an inn room or hospitality.
At the end of the rest scene, each PC may create a Bond, add an emotion to a Bond or swap an emotion. Immediate threats may advance while you rest.
rest.tentText: Created with 4 IP from a single character. Fits the whole group.
rest.hospText: Someone friendly takes the group in, usually for help or money.
rest.safeText: Somewhere with no risk of attack: a consecrated temple, a secret room, a magic circle...

item.name: Use an inventory item
item.desc: Spend IP from a single character to create the item in the backpack and use it right away. Nothing is kept for later.
item.tonicText: One creature recovers from all status effects.
item.shardText: 10 air, bolt, fire, earth or ice damage to one creature you can see.
item.tentText: Lets the group rest in the wilds.

restock.name: Restock IP
restock.desc: In villages, towns and other places with shops, each IP recovered costs 10 zenit. IP never exceeds the character's maximum and cannot be shared between characters.
restock.prompt: Who restocks, and how many IP?

services.name: Travel services
services.desc: Passage for one day of travel, per person. Price and availability depend on the world, and a vehicle may increase the distance of a travel day.

newPlace.name: New place on the map
newPlace.desc: Spend 1 Fabula Point to add an element to the story: a new place on the map (a village, a ruin, a shortcut...). Describe it; the GM decides how and where it appears.
newPlace.prompt: Describe the place the group finds:

explore.name: Scout the area
explore.desc: House rule: the group spends part of the day surveying the region and turns the cards up to 2 away. Counts as one card walked that day.

cartography.name: Cartography
cartography.desc: Camp activity (optional rule). Once before your next rest, after a group travel roll, roll again and keep the new result.

camp.name: Camp activity
camp.desc: Optional rule. In each rest scene, each PC performs one of the two activities they have and applies the benefit to the target. "Once" benefits last until the next rest.
camp.combatText: An ally: once, adds +4 to an Accuracy check or an offensive Magic check.
camp.magicText: An ally: once, casts a spell you know, paying its cost and making the checks.
camp.cartoText: You: once, reroll a group travel roll and keep the new result.
camp.harvestText: A gourmet: roll 1d6. 1: an easy conflict at the end of the rest; 2: 2 random ingredients; 3-5: 3 random; 6: 3 of your choice.
camp.owlText: You: generate 3 progress points for a project.
camp.daydreamText: You: once, when you lose HP, lose only half.
camp.exerciseText: You: once, avoid all status effects you would suffer from a single source.
camp.scoutText: You or an ally: roll 1d6. 1: you recover only half your HP and MP; 2: the target recovers 2 IP; 3-5: 3 IP; 6: 3 IP and you find 50 × your level in zenit.
camp.forgeText: You: repair a group item, create a basic weapon, armor or shield for free, or break equipment down into a material.
camp.massageText: An ally: once, pays half the MP cost (not for rituals).
camp.pepText: An ally: once, doubles the MP they recover.
camp.planText: An ally: once, +4 when leading a group check or examining something or someone.
camp.doubleText: An ally: once, doubles the HP they recover.
camp.sleepText: You: once, one extra action on your turn (Equipment, Hinder or Inventory).
camp.martialText: You: once, when attacking, gain multi (2) or +1 multi.

Sample.chest: An old chest caught between roots. Inside are 300 zenit and a torn map pointing north.
Sample.dungeon: The entrance of a forgotten dungeon, guarded by hollow-eyed statues.
Sample.ruins: Broken columns of a temple. Someone lit a fire here not long ago.

movePermission.name: Who moves the group
movePermission.hint: Players click an adjacent card (or use the arrow keys) and the connected GM validates the step.

flipSound.name: Card flip sound
flipSound.hint: Path of the audio file. Leave empty for no sound.

autoOpen.name: Open the map when the GM shows it
autoOpen.hint: Opens the map automatically when the GM clicks Show to players.

OutcomeHint.danger: The GM describes a danger. The group may avoid it with a group check, a series of checks or, rarely, a conflict.
OutcomeHint.discovery: The group makes an unexpected discovery. Discoveries are always good.
OutcomeHint.calm: Nothing special happens on this travel day.

Chat.treasureHunter: Treasure Hunter: discovery on {max} or less
Chat.dangerHow: A danger should be avoidable with a group check or a series of checks; it rarely becomes a conflict. Damage by group level (core p. 108):
Chat.dangerLocked: The group stays put until you release movement (lock on the map toolbar).
Chat.dayEndText: Threat of the day: {threat} ({die}). Roll the Travel Roll with the Roll button on the map.
Chat.dayEndPlayers: Threat of the day: {threat}. A player rolls the Travel Roll ({die}) with the Roll button on the map. The group travels on after the roll.

New.title: New map
New.name: Name
New.seedHint: The same code, theme and size always make the same map. Write down the code of a map you like.
New.sampleHint: A ready 16 × 10 map with a village, road, forest, river, sea, dungeon and treasure.
New.editHint: Once created, everything can be edited: paint terrain, rename cards, move the group.
New.startVillage: Found a village on the chosen card
New.startHint: Click a card in the preview to choose where the group starts.

ThemeDesc.continent: Land surrounded by sea, with mountains, forests, rivers and roads linking the villages to a city.
ThemeDesc.archipelago: Islands scattered across the sea. Sea routes link the ports: those sea cards can be crossed.
ThemeDesc.desert: Sand as far as the eye can see, oases, rocky ridges and more ruins than usual.
ThemeDesc.frozen: Frozen wastes, pine forests and a cold sea to the north. Few villages.
ThemeDesc.wilds: Dense woods, jungle to the south, swamps and many rivers. Few villages.

Gen.dungeon1: A staircase goes down into the dark. The air rising from it is cold and damp.
Gen.dungeon2: Iron gates stand ajar on a hillside. There are fresh claw marks in the dirt.
Gen.dungeon3: A tower sunk into the ground, only its top showing. A light flickers inside.
Gen.treasure1: A half-buried chest bearing the crest of a forgotten noble house.
Gen.treasure2: A smuggler's cache: bags of coins and a letter with instructions.
Gen.treasure3: An ancient offering on a stone altar. No one has touched it in centuries.
Gen.ruins1: The fallen walls of a fortress. Someone camped here not long ago.
Gen.ruins2: Faceless statues ring an empty square. The wind carries a distant song.
Gen.ruins3: A temple split in two. Its inscriptions speak of a seal and a key.

Config.title: Configure map
Config.name: Name
Config.sizeHint: Growing adds plains cards; shrinking deletes the cards that no longer fit.
Config.revealRadiusHint: After each step, turns the cards within this distance of the group (0 = only the card the group stands on).
Config.movesPerDayHint: How many cards the group walks in one travel day. The roll uses the highest threat among the day's cards.
Config.lockOnDangerHint: On a danger, the group only walks again when the GM releases it.
Config.tablesHint: Optional. Drop a table from the sidebar; it is drawn on a danger or a discovery.
Config.wayfarerHint: Tick what some PC has (core p. 176-177).
Config.veteran: Well-Traveled (die one size smaller, minimum d6)
Config.treasureHunter: Treasure Hunter (discovery on SL + 1 or less)
Config.practical: Resourceful (reminder: recover SL IP after each roll)
Config.rollBy_auto: Automatic, at the end of each day
Config.rollByHint: With the GM or the players, a Roll button appears in the map's status line at the end of the day, and the group only travels on after the roll. The GM can always roll.
Config.lookfarHint: Opens the Lookfar module's Travel Check with the day's die already chosen. Lookfar's roll counts for the map, and Lookfar generates the danger or discovery. Use with The GM or The players in Who rolls.
Config.lookfarMissing: The Lookfar module is not active in this world. With this option on, the map keeps using its own Travel Roll.
Config.actorDrop: Drag an actor here to use its token
Config.partyFrameHint: No frame shows the image as it is, good for tokens with a transparent background.
Config.partyLabelHint: Optional, for example the group's name

Terrains.title: Terrain library
Terrains.intro: Each terrain sets the image, the threat level (the Travel Roll die) and whether it can be crossed. "Name banner" writes the name on the card, as for cities and points of interest.
Terrains.name: Name
Terrains.resetConfirm: Replace the library with the default terrains? Cards of deleted terrains lose their image.

Options.title: Travel options
Options.intro: Cards the players hold while travelling. "Announce in chat" only posts the card; "Travel Roll", "Reroll" and "Turn cards" (value = radius) are run by the GM; "Run macro" runs the macro whose UUID is in the value. "Spends a card of the day" counts as one card walked. Choices: one per line, as Name | cost | effect.
Options.name: Name
Options.step: Spends a card of the day
Options.choices: Choices: Name | cost | effect (one per line)
Options.resetConfirm: Replace every option with the defaults?
